title: Relational Data Model
summary: Tables as sets of tuples; keys (super/candidate/primary/foreign), constraints, and 1:N/M:N/1:1 relationships — the foundation of SQL.

title: Data Models Overview — Relational vs Document vs Key-Value vs Columnar vs Graph
summary: The five data models, how to pick by access pattern, relational-vs-document decision tests, and what Mongoose populate / $lookup really do.

title: Schema Design — ER Diagrams & Normalization (1NF → BCNF)
summary: ER modeling and normalization 1NF→BCNF: functional dependencies, partial/transitive dependencies, the three anomalies, and BCNF's edge case.

title: Denormalization — When and Why to Break Normalization Rules
summary: Trading write complexity for read speed: counter columns, redundant copies, materialized views, consistency strategies, and the decision framework.

title: B-tree Indexes — Structure & How Range/Equality Queries Use Them
summary: How a B-tree turns O(n) scans into O(log n) on-disk lookups; equality vs range traversal, ORDER BY for free, write tax, and why f(column) defeats the index.

title: Composite Indexes — Column Order & the Leftmost-Prefix Rule
summary: The phone-book sort, the leftmost-prefix rule, equality-before-range column ordering, why one composite ≠ two singles, and bitmap/skip scans.

title: Covering Indexes & Index-Only Scans
summary: Answering a query from the index alone: INCLUDE payload columns, eliminating heap fetches, and why Postgres's visibility map / MVCC can still force heap access.

title: Clustered vs Non-clustered Indexes
summary: Rows-in-the-leaf vs pointer-to-heap; the secondary-index double-lookup, Postgres CLUSTER (one-time, decays) vs InnoDB permanent PK clustering, and the clustering factor.

title: Partial & Expression Indexes
summary: Index a subset of rows (partial) or a transformed value (expression); partial UNIQUE for scoped constraints, case-insensitive uniqueness, and combining both.

title: ACID Properties
summary: The four transaction guarantees: WAL-backed atomicity (undo) & durability (redo), why C is the application's job, isolation as a tunable dial, and the wedding-ceremony model.

title: Isolation Levels & Read Anomalies
summary: The anomaly×level table, MVCC snapshot timing per level, Postgres-vs-ANSI divergence, write skew, SSI/predicate locks, and the 40001 retry contract.

title: Two-Phase Locking (2PL)
summary: The growing/shrinking phases and lock-point serializability, S/X compatibility, the Basic→Strict→SS2PL→Conservative variants with a lock-timing trace, and Postgres's MVCC+strict-2PL hybrid.

title: Deadlocks — Detection, Prevention & the Coffman Conditions
summary: The four Coffman conditions as the master key, the four handling strategies, Postgres detect-and-abort (deadlock_timeout, 40P01, consistent lock ordering), and livelock vs deadlock.

title: How Data Is Stored on Disk — Heap Files, Pages & Slots
summary: Heap files → 8 KB pages → line-pointer slots; TID indirection (logical slot vs physical bytes), relfilenode rewrites, forks/TOAST, and the torn-page → full-page-write hazard.

title: MVCC — How Postgres Implements Multi-Version Concurrency Control
summary: Version-stamped tuples (xmin/xmax/ctid chain), the xmin:xmax:xip snapshot, visibility rules + clog, hint bits (reads that write), HOT updates, and the OldestXmin horizon.

title: Table Bloat & Autovacuum — Reclaiming What MVCC Leaves Behind
summary: Dead tuples → bloat; plain VACUUM (reusable, FSM) vs VACUUM FULL/pg_repack (shrink), the VM's two bits, freezing & XID wraparound, and autovacuum triggers/tuning.

title: Write-Ahead Log (WAL) — Crash Recovery & the Durability Guarantee
summary: Log-first rule, LSN/pd_lsn recovery replay (idempotent), checkpoints & redo point, full-page writes vs torn pages, synchronous_commit, redo-only WAL, and PITR/replication.

title: Buffer Pool / Page Cache — How a DB Manages Memory
summary: 8KB pages cached in shared_buffers; buffer table/descriptors, clock-sweep eviction (approx LRU), WAL-flush-before-dirty-write, ring buffers, and double buffering vs the OS cache.

title: How the Internet Works End-to-End — A Packet's Journey
summary: A packet's full journey from browser to server and back: DNS, ARP, encapsulation, TCP/TLS handshakes, hop-by-hop routing, and why the network is best-effort.

title: OSI 7-Layer Model — What Each Layer Does and Why the Split Exists
summary: The seven layers and why layering exists; PDUs, the L2-vs-L3 (switch-vs-router) distinction, OSI-vs-TCP/IP reality check, and the L2/L3/L4/L7 vocabulary.

title: TCP/IP Model — How the 4/5-Layer Model Maps to Reality vs OSI
summary: The real stack the internet runs on: 4- vs 5-layer, the OSI→TCP/IP mapping, where TLS/sockets sit, and the hourglass/narrow-waist model.

title: Encapsulation & Decapsulation — Segments → Packets → Frames → Bits
summary: Dolls-in-dolls header wrapping/unwrapping: PDU names, load-bearing header fields, demultiplexing pointers, router re-encap per hop, and header overhead.

title: Bandwidth vs Throughput vs Latency vs Jitter
summary: The four performance words precisely: rates vs times, the highway model, bandwidth≠speed, latency-bound vs bandwidth-bound, BDP, and jitter/QoS.

title: Ethernet — Frame Format, MAC Addresses & EtherType
summary: The L2 reality: 48-bit MACs (OUI + device, broadcast/unicast/multicast), the frame format, EtherType demux, FCS best-effort error detection, and the 1500-byte MTU.

title: How Switches Work — MAC Learning, CAM Table, Forward/Flood/Filter
summary: Self-teaching frame forwarding: learn from SOURCE, decide by DESTINATION; forward/flood/filter, the CAM table, one-switch-one-broadcast-domain, and CAM overflow.

title: VLANs — Segmentation, Access vs Trunk Ports, 802.1Q Tagging
summary: Slicing one switch into many virtual switches: access vs trunk, the 4-byte 802.1Q tag, tag add/strip journey, native-VLAN hopping, and VLAN-scoped flooding.

title: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP/RSTP) — Loop Prevention & Root Bridge Election
summary: Why L2 loops are fatal (no TTL → broadcast storm) and how STP blocks them: root-bridge election, root/designated/blocking ports, path cost, and RSTP's fast convergence.

title: ARP — Resolving IP → MAC, ARP Cache, Gratuitous ARP
summary: The glue between IP and MAC: broadcast request / unicast reply, next-hop-only resolution, caching, gratuitous ARP for failover, and why ARP spoofing enables MITM.

title: IPv4 Addressing — Structure, Classes (Historical) & Private Ranges (RFC 1918)
summary: The 32-bit address split into network+host by a mask; why classful died (Class B exhaustion, routing-table growth), CIDR + longest-prefix match, RFC 1918 blocks, and the special-purpose registry.

title: Subnetting — CIDR Notation, Masks & Calculating Subnets by Hand
summary: Borrowing host bits to split a network: RFC 950's origin and the locality principle, the block-size method, design in both directions, the .0/.255 trap, and subnet zero.

title: VLSM & Route Summarization — Carving a Network Efficiently
summary: Sizing each subnet to its real requirement: why fixed-length can be impossible, the alignment rule and largest-first procedure, why VLSM needs a classless protocol, and summarization as the inverse.

title: Routing Fundamentals — The Routing Table, Longest-Prefix Match & Next Hop
summary: A router's one job and the table that answers it: the RFC 1812 forwarding algorithm, LPM as primary key (not a tiebreak), AD vs metric, recursive next-hop resolution, host routing, and the RIB/FIB split.

title: SELECT FOR UPDATE & SKIP LOCKED — Row Locks and the Postgres Job Queue
summary: Read-and-reserve via row-level exclusive locks: the lost-update race MVCC leaves open, the four lock strengths + conflict matrix, wait/NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED policies, the CTE job-queue claim, and READ COMMITTED's EvalPlanQual re-check.

title: Advisory Locks — Application-Level Coordination Through the Database
summary: Locks on application-invented integers that guard code, not data: the sign-up-sheet model, the singleton-cron case row locks can't solve, session-vs-transaction scope, the try/shared function matrix, key-space collisions, and the LIMIT dangling-lock trap.

title: Optimistic vs Pessimistic Locking — Choosing by Conflict Rate and Window Length
summary: Two answers to the application-level lost update: lock-first vs validate-at-write; Kung & Robinson's read/validate/write phases, why the version column is a compare-and-swap built on EvalPlanQual, the READ COMMITTED (0 rows) vs REPEATABLE READ (40001) split, the atomic-in-place third option, and the per-row blind spot (write skew, phantoms).

title: SQL Fundamentals — Joins, Aggregations, Subqueries & CTEs
summary: Logical evaluation order as the master key; the cross-product join model with the ON-vs-WHERE silent-inner-join and fan-out double-counting traps, LATERAL top-N; GROUP BY grain change, WHERE-vs-HAVING, aggregate NULL skipping and FILTER; the NOT IN NULL trap vs NOT EXISTS; and CTEs with the Postgres 12 inlining rule, the recursive working-table algorithm, and one-snapshot data-modifying CTEs.

title: Window Functions — RANK, ROW_NUMBER, LAG/LEAD, Partitions & Frames
summary: Aggregate without collapsing the row: why window functions can't appear in WHERE (they run after it) and the CTE-wrapper that follows; ROW_NUMBER/RANK/DENSE_RANK tie behaviour and top-N-per-group; LAG/LEAD with the flag-then-running-SUM sessionization and gaps-and-islands idioms; and frames — the RANGE default, peer groups, the stalled running total, the LAST_VALUE trap, and ROWS-vs-RANGE as 'last 7 rows' vs 'last 7 days'.

title: Join Algorithms — Nested Loop, Hash Join & Merge Join
summary: Three answers to one lookup question: nested loop (O(N*M), but O(N*log M) and unbeatable with a small indexed inner side — and structurally the N+1 in the right place), hash join (O(N+M), equality only, with the work_mem x hash_mem_multiplier cliff and Batches>1 spill signal), and merge join (free when an index supplies the order, and the only other option for range joins); plus the row-estimate cliff that makes a wrong nested loop degrade without bound, the enable_* switches as diagnostics, and geqo join ordering.

title: Query Planning & Optimization — How the Database Picks a Plan
summary: The planner as a search engine with a cost function, not a translator: the parser/rewriter/planner/executor path (and why a view is a pre-planning substitution), paths vs plans, the startup..total cost pair that explains LIMIT flips, cost as arithmetic on top of cardinality, the System R bottom-up search and the geqo threshold, the transformations it applies for you, the six things it cannot do, and the estimate-vs-cost-model split that decides every fix.

title: EXPLAIN & EXPLAIN ANALYZE — Reading Query Plans in Practice
summary: Reading intent against reality: the node anatomy, costs being cumulative upward and actual time/rows being per-loop averages that must be multiplied by loops, the diagnostic order (find the LOWEST node where estimated and actual rows diverge), the scan-node vocabulary including Bitmap Heap Scan and Heap Fetches, the BUFFERS/SETTINGS/GENERIC_PLAN options, and a worked plan traced from a 4000x top-level gap down to the composite index that actually fixes it.
